steps: Codes, location & clearances
Install to CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or ANSI Z223.1 (USA) and local codes, using qualified personnel. Plan the unit, vent path and gas piping together and hold the clearances in Figures 3 & 4.

• Qualified (licensed or trained) personnel only; in Massachusetts, only a licensed plumber and gas fitter. Venting and installation to the current CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or National Fuel Gas Code ANSI Z223.1 (USA), approved per local codes.
  • Possible locations: an existing wall, a corner, a built-in wall or a wall projection (Figure 9). Not in high-traffic areas or near furniture or draperies.
  • Manufactured (mobile) homes: where local codes allow, after the "first sale"; the fireplace must be fastened in place. CAN/CSA Z240 MH (Canada); Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 or ANSI/NFPA 501A (USA).
  • Massachusetts side-wall venting with the termination less than seven (7) feet above grade: 248 CMR 5.08 hard-wired CO detector with alarm and battery back-up on the appliance floor, detectors on each other level, and a "Gas vent directly below. Keep clear of all obstructions" sign at least eight (8) feet above grade (p. 4).
  • Never connect it to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance. Suitable for a bedroom or bed sitting room.
Remove the door, fit top standoffs

With the unit off and cool, lift off the safety barrier screen, release both spring latches with the one-piece handle, then tilt the door frame out and lift it off its bottom track. Install the loose top standoffs once the fireplace is in position.

1. Pry the top of the safety barrier screen toward you, then lift it off its tabs at the base of the door frame.
  2. Remove the TC Finishing Touch Trim Kit from the door frame, if installed.
  3. Push a screwdriver against the notch at the top of the latch, grab the bottom of the latch handle as it protrudes and lift until the hook disengages. Repeat on the other side while supporting the door so it can't tip out.
  4. Tilt the top of the frame out past the top edge of the unit, then lift it up and out of its bottom track. Store it safely.

Reassemble in reverse: the latch handle snaps in flush with the frame. Check by grasping the top left and right of the frame: under moderate pressure it should pull forward and return evenly on both sides. The ceramic glass is very fragile.

Top standoffs ship loose inside the fireplace; install them on top (Figure 8, p. 8) once it's in position.
Position & arched framing kit
With the fireplace in its final spot and the venting in, assemble the supplied arched steel stud framing kit TC36.BRFRKITA and fix it to the unit's framing brackets and the house framing.

1. On a large flat surface lay out the inner (2) and outer (3) side studs and the centre studs (4); screw the upper header (5) and stud plate (6) to the centre studs.
  2. Attach the side studs to the top of the header and fasten them at the bottom with the base plates (7).
  3. Archway: attach the diagonal studs (9) to the lower horizontal studs and the inner vertical studs. Turn the frame over for the remaining fastening points.
  4. Align the frame to the unit's framing brackets and fasten through the access holes in the outer side studs, screw-hole side facing the fireplace.
  5. Secure it to the existing framing through the upper horizontal stud and the stud plates.
  6. Install the non-combustible board with drywall screws.

The lintel is fixed, so its front face sets the fireplace's final position. The framing brackets give 1 7/8" of adjustment: allow for the facing thickness (1/2" calcium silicate board or rock) first. Arch kit: 66 Tek screws, 48" inner and outer side studs, 49 7/8" header, 41 1/4" stud plate, 5 15/16" base plates, 4 framing plates, 2 arch supports. Arch minimum combustible framing dimensions are a dimensioned drawing (Figure 12, p. 10).
Board, facing & hearth

Sheet the front in non-combustible board 12" above and 5 9/16" to the sides of the framing edges. Finish flush (facing up to 1 7/8") or with a 4 1/2" recess, never blocking the door or screen, and keep any hearth to no more than 1" above the bottom of the fireplace.
Power, wall switch & vent mode

Connect 110 V AC in the junction box behind the right-side firebox access panel, then mount the wall switch, continuity-check its 40 ft cable, connect it to the interface board and load the 4 AA batteries. Set the PV / NV switch for the vent system.

1. Fireplace in place; remove the glass door frame and the access panel on the right side of the firebox.
  2. Connect 110 V AC to the wires inside the junction box (Figure 29).
  3. Attach the wall switch to the framing, route the supplied control cable, and connect one end to the wall control and the other to the interface board (Figure 30).
  4. Insert the 4 supplied "AA" batteries into the wall switch battery pack.
  5. If not already installed, install the burner using the instructions supplied with the burner kit.
  6. Turn on the gas and electrical supplies; check that all connections are tight and leak free.

Check the continuity of each wire in the communication cable before plugging it in at either end and before it's walled in. With home automation, two cables leave the wall switch (top to the fireplace, bottom to the home automation system); otherwise only the upper one is used.

PV / NV switch on the interface board: NV without a power vent, PV with one (follow the power vent kit's instructions). To change it, turn off the electrical supply and remove the backup batteries to reset the module.
Gas supply & pressure check

Bring the line to the 3/8" N.P.T. valve inlet through a union or flare fitting (never hard piped), with a sediment trap no more than 6 feet from the valve, and check that every connection is tight and leak free. Verify supply and manifold pressures with the fireplace lit on its highest setting.
Vent & terminate

Use approved Town & Country vent components and only the 22270012 wall or 22270010 roof termination kit; hold 1 3/4" to combustibles, rise ¼" per foot of horizontal run, and screw and tape every joint. Finish with the insulated collar shield (TC36.9709) flush with the top of the unit.

Wall termination

  • Frame a 14½" opening (round or square) centred at least 68½" above the floor, between framing members if possible. The vent kit takes walls up to 12" thick.
  • Through a combustible wall, fit the wall thimble/shield (22270011) from inside, trimmed to the wall thickness including siding, flush with the outer wall.
  • Neither thimble nor vent may protrude beyond the siding, and the terminal must not be recessed into the wall or siding. Engage both inner and outer pipes fully, attach the terminal to the wall and caulk it.

Roof termination

  • Frame 14 ½" openings in floors, ceilings and roof; the roof opening grows with pitch to keep the 1¾" air space. Avoid cutting rafters.
  • Ceiling firestop (22270011) at each floor or ceiling, pushed up from below. Into an attic, leave its shield full length (attic insulation shield 22270029 may be required) and put a storm collar on top of it.
  • Roof support bracket (80001286) to the joists, flashing (22220002 adjustable, 22220003 flat, 22220004 steep, or any flashing that fits 11" pipe), storm collar (80000472) with a thick ring of mastic, then the vertical termination cap (80000574), screwed and caulked.
  • Pipe at least 12" above the roof, more on steeper roofs (Roof Pitch Table, minimum):
Flat to 6/121.00 ft
Over 6/12 to 7/121.25 ft
Over 7/12 to 8/121.50 ft
Over 8/12 to 9/122.00 ft
Over 9/12 to 10/122.50 ft
Over 10/12 to 11/123.25 ft
Over 11/12 to 12/124.00 ft
The roof termination kit drawing (Figure 55, p. 31) prints the roof support bracket as 800001286; Figure 45 (p. 26) gives 80001286.

Wrap the supplied high-temperature self-adhesive aluminium tape fully around every outer joint and press it firm. Terminal clearances are on p. 28; vent offsets are a dimensioned drawing (Figure 58, p. 33).
Set the vent restrictor
Read the restrictor opening for your vent height and horizontal length off the chart (Figure 51), set it, and fine-tune by the flame. It must be fully open with a power vent.

The restrictor sits on the underside of the firebox top and adjusts secondary air, tuning flame appearance and performance to the vent configuration. The unit leaves the factory with it open. Chart positions are based on lab tests and the ideal one may vary slightly; the chart is a rise-and-run graph, so read the opening from the page (Figure 51, p. 30).

  1. Determine the vent height and the horizontal vent length.
  2. Find the restrictor position on the chart.
  3. Loosen the screws holding the restrictor plates, move the plates to the opening and retighten.
  • Closed too much: flame excessively tall and lifting, lacks movement, or soots.
  • Too open: flame height low, or excessive flame movement.
The vent restrictor must be fully open when using the power vent.
Install the firebox panels (Arch)

Remove the five-screw brow piece, fit the one-piece rear panel, make the gas connection, then the right and left side panels, the brow piece and the front panels. A panel set must be installed before the fireplace is used.

1. Remove the brow piece from the underside of the firebox heat shield (five screws behind its front flange, Figure 63).
  2. Install the one-piece lower rear panel.
  3. Make the gas connection before installing the panels.
  4. Right side panel: insert the bottom first, then angle it up into position (push the firebox shield up if needed).
  5. Left side panel, the same way.
  6. Reinstall the brow piece.
  7. Install the left and right front panels.

A panel set must be installed for safe operation, before the logs are in place. Panels are very fragile: unpack and inspect them first. Because of supplier manufacturing tolerances, fibre panels may need trimming to fit. Porcelain panels have their own instruction manual; see the burner instructions before starting. The Arch's one-piece rear panel has no "V" brackets.

Trim, barrier screen & pairing
Fit transition trim kit 80002253 and the magnetic safety barrier screen, then pair the wall switch to the fireplace and the remote to the wall switch.

Transition trim kit 80002253 (Arch)

  1. With the door in place, put two smaller magnets on the back of each side trim piece and three larger magnets on the back of the top piece.
  2. Attach the side pieces first (there's a left and a right; the smaller tab goes to the top) and even their ends with the door frame.
  3. Attach the top piece and adjust it so the mitres are even at the corners.
  4. Rest the meshed bottom piece on the floor in the gap between the frame and the glass door; affix the Town & Country badge to its right-hand side.
  5. Attach the magnetic safety barrier screen to the outer-most door frame.

Pairing (Bluetooth wall switch)

Selector to "Remote"; hold the Program button (straightened paper clip) for up to 10 seconds until the wall switch beeps 5 times, then release; the fireplace beeps 3 times, then another 3. Next press and release Program once (3 beeps) and, within 60 sec., press and release on/off on the remote: 3 beeps confirm. If a nearby fireplace responds instead, repeat the first procedure to move to another of three channels. With the basic wall switch the remote pairs directly to the module (module beeps, p. 40).

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: an ignition device lights the pilot automatically. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Before you light it

Smell all around the fireplace for gas, and right next to the floor too, because some gas is heavier than air and settles low. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety.

Lighting steps

  1. Push the On/Off switch to turn the fireplace on. The On/Off key on the remote and the On/Off switch on the wall switch both turn it on and off.
  2. If the burner lights, set the flame you want with the hand-held remote.
  3. If it doesn't light, push the On/Off switch to off and wait at least 5 minutes so any gas in the firebox can clear.
  4. Still smell gas? Stop and follow the gas-smell steps. No smell? Go back to step 1.
The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light each time. The very first time, air also has to clear out of the gas lines, so give it time.
Won't light or stay lit after several tries? Push the On/Off switch to off, turn off all electric power to the fireplace and call your service technician or gas supplier.

Turning it off

Push the On/Off switch to off. Before service, or for a long shutdown, also turn off all electric power to it and take out the backup batteries.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
Your remote is a Proflame 2 handset with a blue back-lit screen. It runs on 3 AAA batteries and has an On/Off key, a Thermostat key, up and down arrows and a Mode key. One beep from the fireplace means it got your command.

On and off

Press On/Off. When the fireplace is off, the screen shows only the room temperature.

Flame height

There are six flame levels. Each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one step, until the flame goes out. The up arrow raises it. If the fireplace is on but the flame is out, the up arrow brings it back on high.

Light dimmer

Press Mode until the light bulb icon shows, then use the arrows to pick one of six light levels.

Key lock

Press Mode and the up arrow together to lock the keys; a lock icon appears. Press both together again to unlock.

Remote not working? Turn the fireplace on or off with the On/Off switch on the wall switch instead.

The thermostat feature comes switched off. The manual says it isn't permitted in the USA.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
A smell the first few hours

The first time it's lit, the fireplace gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours. It comes from the paints, sealants and lubricants used in manufacturing as they cure. It's temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room, since the odor can bother some people.

Ticks and pops

Steel fireplaces make some expansion and contraction noises as they warm up and cool down. That's normal, much like the sounds from your furnace or your oven.

A pause before it lights

The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light each time you turn the fireplace on.

Beeps

One beep means the fireplace received a command from the remote. A double-beep means its backup batteries are low; see Power outages & batteries.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches or use any phone in your building, and call your gas supplier from a neighbour's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it, using fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Only clean the glass when it's cool. Hot glass will cause burns.
  • Never use abrasive cleaners on the glass or on any other part of the fireplace.
  • The outside finish cleans up with mild soap and water.
  • Don't strike or knock the glass in any way that could break it.

Cracked or broken glass

Don't use the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken. It has to be replaced first, and a licensed or qualified service person should do it. Replacement glass comes from your Town & Country dealer: tell them yours is the TC36 Arch, with the arched door. Only ceramic glass can be used.

If the door ever has to come off, the steps are under Door Frame Removal in the installation manual (p. 7). Turn the fireplace off and let it cool fully first. The ceramic glass is very fragile.

pilot.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
pilot.html:
The fireplace's control module lights the pilot automatically and keeps watch on the pilot flame. You can choose between two pilot modes:

IPIIntermittent pilot ignition
CPIContinuous pilot ignition

To switch modes

  1. Make sure the fireplace is off.
  2. Press Mode on the remote until the CPI icon shows.
  3. Press the up arrow to turn on continuous pilot (CPI), or the down arrow to go back to intermittent pilot (IPI). One beep confirms.

In either mode, never try to light the pilot by hand. Each time you turn the fireplace on, the pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on household power. A battery pack in the wall switch is its backup.

Wall switch backup pack4 AA batteries
Remote3 AAA batteries

In a power outage

The backup batteries power the fireplace's control only when house power is interrupted or lost, and only if your fireplace doesn't use a power vent.

Low-battery signs

  • Remote: a battery icon appears on its screen before the power runs out, and goes away once you put in new batteries.
  • Backup pack: the fireplace double-beeps when it gets a command. With fresh batteries it's back to a single beep.

How long batteries last depends on their quality, how often the fireplace lights, and similar things.

Changing batteries? The manual says to turn off the main gas supply to the fireplace before you remove or put back the batteries.
Shutting it down for a long time? Turn off the electric power to it and take out the backup batteries.

app.title: The TC Fire app & pairing
app.html:
Besides the remote, you can run the fireplace from a phone over Bluetooth with the free TC Fire app (Apple App Store or Google Play). The app turns the flame and the light on and off, and its sliders set their levels.

Pairing, in this order

  1. Wall switch to fireplace: set the wall switch selector to Remote. With a straightened paper clip, press and hold its Program button for up to 10 seconds, until it beeps 5 times, then let go. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more.
  2. Remote to wall switch: press and release Program once (3 beeps). Within 60 seconds, press and release On/Off on the remote. The wall switch beeps 3 times.
  3. Phone (optional): in the app, go to Add/Edit Fireplace and press Add. Enter the PIN from the sticker on the wall switch and a name for the fireplace, then press Save.
Another nearby fireplace comes on instead? Repeat step 1. It switches to another of three channels.

Your phone only shows the saved fireplace when it's within Bluetooth range and no one else is controlling it.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbour's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Hot glass and children

Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. The barrier that came with the fireplace must be installed to protect children and others at risk. Watch young children closely in the same room; a safety gate can keep toddlers away from hot surfaces.

Around the fireplace

  • Keep furniture, drapes, clothing and anything flammable away from it.
  • Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Put back any panel or door removed for service before you use it.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • Don't use it if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
  • Don't try to repair it yourself. Contact your dealer.

service.title: Yearly service & light bulb
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the fireplace and its venting before first use and at least once a year. Town & Country recommends technicians certified by the National Fireplace Institute (NFI) as NFI Gas Specialists. Lint from carpets or bedding can mean cleaning more often.

The yearly check

  1. Glass off; decorative media (logs, pebbles, glass) checked for soot and cleaned; burner brushed or vacuumed, especially the ports. Heavy soot means the unit needs adjusting for proper combustion.
  2. Pilot flame size and operation checked; pilot cleaned.
  3. Vent pipe and vent terminal checked for blockage or debris.
  4. Glass gasket checked and replaced if needed.
  5. Batteries checked and replaced as needed.

Changing the light bulb

With the gas and power off and the fireplace cool, remove the screw holding the light cover in the top of the firebox and lower the light a little. Pop the glass lens open with a small flat screwdriver and wiggle the old bulb out of its plug. Hold the new bulb (a 20W halogen) in a paper towel or cloth, because skin oils make bulbs fail early; if you touch it, clean it with alcohol. Push it in, close the lens and refit the screw.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Town & Country's limited lifetime warranty for gas products covers the original registered purchaser.

Glass (thermal breakage only), combustion chamber, burner tube assembly, porcelain finishesLimited lifetime, parts only
Any defective part2 years, parts and labor, from the original purchase date

Conditions

  • Installed by a qualified technician, following local and national requirements and the appliance manual, with a sediment trap within 6 feet of the gas valve. The installer makes sure it fires as the rating plate says.
  • Defective parts are repaired, replaced or refunded at Town & Country's option, which may refund the wholesale price of the part instead.
  • Porcelain is warranted for gloss retention. Some colors darken when hot and return to their shade when cool.

Not covered

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accidents or lack of maintenance.
  • Mantels, surrounds or finishing material around the fireplace.
  • Conditions beyond Town & Country's control, and special, indirect or consequential damages beyond the purchase price.
Not following the manual's installation or operating instructions voids the warranty. This is a summary; the full terms are in the owner's manual.

specSupply.title: Supply pressure & gas connection
specSupply.html:
Natural gas min / max5.0" / 13.9" WC
Propane min / max12.5" / 13.9" WC

The minimum is for the purpose of input adjustment. Verify gas pressures with the fireplace lit and on its highest setting; turn the gas supply off before removing the plug from the supply or manifold test port (Figure 38). The test procedure itself is in the burner installation manual.

Gas connection

  • Valve inlet accepts a 3/8" N.P.T. fitting; supply line access holes are at the top and left sides of the control box. Use the correct line diameter for proper operation and pressure.
  • Sediment trap, per the National Fuel Gas Code, no more than 6 feet from the gas control valve.
  • Don't hard pipe to the valve: provide a union or flare fitting so the valve can be repaired or replaced.
  • Supply piping tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve. At 1/2 psig or less: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Reinstall the access panel and its gasket after installation, conversion or service, or the control system will overheat and fail early.

J · non-mechanical air supply inlet, or another appliance's combustion air inlet12" (30 cm) *
K · mechanical air supply inlet6 feet (1.8 m) *
L · above a paved sidewalk or driveway on public property7 feet (2.1 m) *
M · under a veranda, porch, deck or balcony30" (76 cm) **

All minimums, measured to the nearest edge of the termination hood. * As specified in CGA B149; U.S.A. installations follow the current National Fuel Gas Code, ANSI Z223.1. ** Only if the veranda, porch, deck or balcony is fully open on a minimum of 2 sides beneath the floor. L: never terminate directly above a sidewalk or paved driveway between two single family dwellings that serves both. The terminal must not be recessed, and local codes may require different clearances.

specFrame.title: Framing, facing & hearth
specFrame.html:
Arched steel stud framing kit (supplied)TC36.BRFRKITA
Non-combustible board12" above and 5 9/16" to the sides of the framing edges
Calcium silicate board1/2" thick
Facing, flush installup to 1 7/8" thick
Framing bracket adjustment1 7/8"
Recess with non-combustible masonry-type materialup to 4 1/2"
Hearth extension (optional)1" max. above the bottom of the fireplace
  • The fireplace should be in its final position, with venting installed, before framing; its fixed lintel's front face sets that position.
  • The steel stud kit must be used unless the unit is totally enclosed in non-combustible material. No combustible material, electrical wiring, insulation, plastic vapor barrier or gas plumbing within the steel stud framing; a full header above it is highly recommended.
  • Sides, back and top can be framed in conventional lumber up to the steel studs and standoffs. Standard drywall may be used beyond the non-combustible board.
  • Unless the board will be finished with tiles or other non-combustible material, make its top section a single sheet of calcium silicate board (taped and mudded joints may crack). Pre-drill its mounting holes. Painting the wall above? Discard the framing kit and use full sheets of calcium silicate board and full-length metal studs.
  • 3/4" facing finishes flush with the front of the unit (p. 9); flush installs accept facing up to 1 7/8" (p. 15). Facing must never stop the door or screen from opening, including in the event of ignition of excess gas buildup.
  • Deeper recesses than 4 1/2" are allowed if the facing is moved away from the unit and window, top and sides, at a ratio of 1:1, up to a maximum 12" deep (p. 11).
  • A hearth extension isn't required and combustible flooring may run up to the unit, but wood flooring may discolor, shrink or crack. Thicker than 1": raise the fireplace accordingly, or it will interfere with the screen and door.
  • Against an uninsulated exterior wall or chase: insulate it like other exterior walls, cover insulation and vapour barrier with drywall, don't place the unit against insulation, and seal the chase at the ceiling or between floors.

Arch minimum combustible framing dimensions are a dimensioned drawing (Figure 12, p. 10); fireplace dimensions are Figure 2 (p. 5).

specElec.title: Electrical & controls
specElec.html:
Fireplace110 volts, 60Hz, 0.25A
Optional power vent kit115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A
Wall switch communication cable40 ft. (supplied)
Wall switch backup batteries4 "AA" (supplied)
LightHalogen light bulb 20W (80002650)
  • 110 V AC goes to the wires inside the junction box (Figure 29), reachable from inside or outside the box through either small access panel. The gas control system sits on the right side of the firebox behind an access panel and the decorative firebox panel (if installed).
  • Check the continuity of each wire in the communication cable before plugging it into the wall switch and the IFC module, and before it's walled in.
  • PV / NV switch on the interface board: NV without a power vent, PV with one. When switching, turn off the electrical power and remove the backup batteries to reset the module.
  • Home automation (Bluetooth wall switch): flame and light on/off through a dry contact relay; flame and light level through a 0 - 10 volt DC signal (Low = 1 volt, High = 10 volts). The control repeats a signal every 2 hours or until a new command arrives. A second cable runs from the wall switch to the system (wire not supplied).
  • Basic wall switch home automation: flame on and off only, through a dry contact relay on the solid brown wire and common.
  • Backup batteries are used only when line power is lost, and only if the fireplace doesn't use a power vent (owner's manual p. 7).

Wiring diagram: Figure 81 (p. 45).

Note: p. 16 rates the optional power vent kit at 115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A; the rating label on p. 46 lists a blower electrical rating of 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A beside the optional power vent kits.

review.notes: Input rates, efficiency (P.4.1-15 26.8%) and altitude come only from the rating label (install p. 46); the NG/LP column order of the minimum inputs (32,000 NG / 38,000 LP) was confirmed from the layout text, where the values sit under the NATURAL GAS and LP GAS headers. Drawings not transcribed (rule 4): the mantel clearance chart (Figure 3, p. 6) lists clearances A 9", B 6", C 3" and mantel depths D 12", E 6 3/4", F 1 1/2", but which depth goes with which clearance (and the reference line) is only in the drawing, so the guide gives just the rating label's 9" mantel / 12" maximum extension and points to p. 6; also left as page pointers: fireplace dimensions (Fig. 2, p. 5), Arch minimum combustible framing (Fig. 12, p. 10), steel stud kit outline (Fig. 10, p. 9), roof opening A/B sizes by pitch (p. 26), vent pipe dimensions (p. 32), vent offsets (Fig. 58, p. 33), the vent restrictor rise/run chart (Fig. 51, p. 30; only the flame symptoms and procedure are used), terminal clearance drawings (Figs. 47-48, p. 28; the A-M text list is used) and the wiring diagram (p. 45). Not treated as conflicts: 3/4" facing 'will allow' a flush finish (p. 9) vs facing up to 1 7/8" for a flush install (p. 15, with the 1 7/8" framing bracket range on p. 14); recess 'up to 4 1/2"' (p. 6) vs deeper recesses allowed with a 1:1 facing setback to 12" (p. 11); Series D2 (install cover) = 'Series D - version 2' (owner cover) = 'D' (rating label); model codes TC36AR / TC36ARCH / TC36D2 ARCH. Cross-reference errors in the manuals: install p. 17 points to the pairing steps on 'page 38/39' (they are on pp. 39-40); the owner's manual TOC lists the warranty on p. 21 but it starts on p. 20. Pages with no text (footer only): install p. 47 and owner pp. 21-23, so if the warranty continues there it is image-only and wasn't read. Lighting label item C (use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob, never use tools, force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion) is in the Safety drawer as printed, although the lighting steps use the On/Off switch and neither manual otherwise describes a manual valve knob; the label doesn't say which On/Off switch it means, so the light drawer names the remote's On/Off key and the wall switch's On/Off switch (both turn it on and off per owner p. 8). IPI/CPI: the owner's manual only names the modes (intermittent / continuous pilot ignition) and gives the switching steps, so the guide doesn't describe how each behaves. Owner p. 7 mentions Proflame 2 comfort-fan control (six speeds), but neither manual describes a fan or blower kit for this model, so there's no blower content. The thermostat function is disabled by default and 'not permissible in the USA' (owner p. 6); the Canada-only enabling steps are left out. The burner (catalog 'Design-A-Fire') has its own installation manual, referenced for burner installation and the gas pressure test procedure (install pp. 16, 20, 34), which is not among the inputs: no burner, media or log content in the guide. Wording: 'fibre panels made need to be trimmed to fit' (p. 34) rendered as 'may need trimming'. Door removal names a 'TC Finishing Touch Trim Kit' (p. 7); the trim section calls the Arch kit Transition Trim Kit 80002253 (p. 36). Power vent part numbers on p. 21 (22270003, 22270004, 22270013) and the kit codes on the rating label (TCVT.PVI.25, TCVT.PV7.110, TCVT.PVCV, TCVT.PVVT) can't be matched; power-vent venting is in separate manuals not provided. Catalog items the manuals don't cover: view area 941 sq in; power venting 'up to 110 ft from an exterior wall'. Catalog features say battery backup keeps it running in an outage, but the owner's manual (p. 7) limits battery backup to units without a power vent; catalog 'switched to standing pilot' corresponds to CPI (continuous pilot ignition) in the manual. The Massachusetts 248 CMR 5.08 side-wall vent rules (p. 4) are summarized only in install step 1.
